title: Coverage is claims-made with a 24-month retroactivity window and a 24-month tail after a role ends
content:
A.2.9.1.1.1.3.6 imports a standard professional-liability structure. Coverage is "Claims made": the Loss Event — receipt of a subpoena, writ, lawsuit, or regulatory communication per A.2.9.1.1.1.3.1 — must occur after the Effective Date, not the conduct. A Retroactivity Period then allows the underlying "facts and circumstances" to have occurred up to 24 months before the later of the Effective Date and first eligibility. A.2.9.1.1.1.3.5 adds the tail: eligibility "expire[s] twenty-four (24) months after cessation of their role as a Beneficiary."

Each boundary answers a specific failure mode. Claims-made triggering means the fund never has to reconstruct when conduct occurred, only when the action arrived. Retroactivity covers the realistic lag between governance work and a regulator noticing it. The tail addresses the structural risk of contributor roles: someone who steps back from Sky remains exposed for years, and a fund that dropped them at exit would fail precisely the people who bore risk on Sky's behalf.

The residual gap is at both edges. Facts older than 24 months before eligibility are uncovered even if the claim is fresh, and an action arriving 25 months after someone leaves is uncovered even though it concerns work done for Sky. Coverage of long-fuse regulatory risk — the kind most likely to materialize slowly — is therefore weakest exactly where crypto enforcement timelines tend to sit.

Geographic coverage is unqualified worldwide (A.2.9.1.1.1.3.4), so jurisdiction is not a limiting dimension; time is.
description: The Loss Event must occur after the Effective Date, its underlying facts may predate eligibility by up to 24 months, and eligibility survives 24 months past cessation of the beneficiary's role.
